general.lead: RailSafe AI is a desktop monitoring system for railway crossings using cameras, AI detection and PLC signals.

blocks.title: In simple words
items: The dashboard shows each crossing as a card with live video, vehicle counts, train status and statistics.
AI detects light and heavy vehicles from the camera image.
If PLC is connected, train approach is shown as a separate safety state.

blocks.title: What is on the main screen?
items: Top toolbar: Dashboard, Add Crossing, Refresh, Settings, Analytics and About.
Crossing card: video, daily vehicle count, train count and PLC state.
Analytics page: daily, weekly and monthly charts plus Word reports.

blocks.title: Operator rule
blocks.text: Add the crossing first, connect the camera, then check polygon and PLC settings. After that the system monitors automatically.

start.lead: An operator who receives the EXE can start with this sequence.

blocks.title: Minimum launch path
items: Open RailSafe.exe and wait for the main window.
On first launch the AI model may prepare for 10-30 seconds; this is normal.
Click + Add Crossing and enter the crossing name and location.
Open the crossing card and add at least one main camera.
Enter the RTSP URL or choose a video file for testing.
Select a polygon file if available, or leave it empty and add it later.
If PLC exists, enter IP and port; otherwise keep PLC disabled for now.
Return to dashboard and check camera status, occupancy and vehicle count.

blocks.title: Be patient on first launch
blocks.text: While the AI model, camera stream or TensorRT engine is preparing, video may be hidden for a while. If the app looks busy, wait 1-2 minutes first.

blocks.title: Ready-to-work checklist
items: Camera is not stuck on Connecting and video is visible.
Light/Heavy/Total numbers change when vehicles pass.
If polygon exists, Occupancy becomes greater than 0 when a vehicle enters the zone.
If PLC is connected, PLC state shows Connected or Train approaching.

crossing.lead: A crossing is one railway crossing monitored by the system. Each crossing has its own cameras, PLC settings and statistics.

blocks.title: Add a crossing
items: Click + Add Crossing on the top toolbar.
Enter a short clear name, for example Crossing 8.
Enter the object location.
Add an optional description if needed.
If PLC is ready, enable it on the PLC Settings tab; otherwise keep it disabled.
Click Save. The crossing appears as a card on the dashboard.

blocks.title: When to add multiple crossings?
blocks.text: If you monitor several real railway crossings or independent checkpoints, add each one as a separate crossing.

blocks.title: Be careful before deleting
blocks.text: Deleting a crossing can remove its camera settings and statistics. Export reports or JSON backup first.

camera.lead: A camera is needed to see the crossing and count vehicles. At least one main camera is recommended.

blocks.title: Add a camera
items: Open the crossing card.
Click + Camera.
Give the camera a name, for example A1 or North direction.
Choose Main or Additional. Main camera is shown in the large view.
Enter the RTSP URL or video file path.
Check that Enable camera and Enable detection are selected.
Click Save and wait for video.

blocks.title: RTSP examples
items: Common format: rtsp://login:password@IP:554/channel
Common Hikvision format: rtsp://admin:password@192.168.1.50:554/Streaming/Channels/101
If it does not open, test the same RTSP URL in VLC Media Player.

blocks.title: Main camera rule
blocks.text: One crossing should have one main camera. Extra cameras are used as additional views or replace the current main camera.

plc.lead: PLC tells the system that a train is approaching. It is shown together with camera occupancy for safety awareness.

blocks.title: Connect PLC
items: Open Add/Edit Crossing and go to PLC Settings.
Enable PLC.
Enter IP address, for example 192.168.170.159.
Port is usually 102 unless your automation specialist gives another value.
Test connection if the button is available, then save.

blocks.title: PLC states
items: CONNECTED - communication works and the system waits for train signal.
TRAIN APPROACHING - PLC active signal is received; operator should watch the crossing zone.
NO CONNECTION - check IP, cable, network or PLC settings.
DISABLED - PLC monitoring is not used for this crossing.

blocks.title: Safety note
blocks.text: The application provides monitoring and warnings. Final safety decisions must follow local rules and responsible staff procedures.

polygon.lead: Polygon is the counting zone inside the camera image. Occupancy and waiting time are calculated when vehicles enter it.

blocks.title: Why polygon is needed
items: Even if the camera sees a wide area, the system counts only the needed road part.
When a vehicle enters the zone, Occupancy increases.
Long waiting inside the zone can produce yellow, orange or red warnings.

blocks.title: Create polygon by drawing (recommended)
items: Camera card → "⋮" → Edit
Click the "✏️ Draw" button next to the polygon file
The camera frame opens (a few seconds to load)
Left click — add zone points (at least 3)
Right click — remove last point; "Clear" — all
"Save" — the polygon is saved as JSON automatically

blocks.title: Color meanings
items: Green - zone is empty or no risk.
Yellow - vehicle is in the zone for a short time.
Orange - warning time threshold was exceeded.
Red - violation threshold was exceeded, or train is approaching while a vehicle is in the zone.

blocks.title: Good polygon rule
blocks.text: Do not make the zone too large. Mark only the road part related to the crossing. Too large gives false occupancy; too small can miss vehicles.

analytics.lead: Analytics page turns collected data into charts and official reports.

blocks.title: What you can see
items: Today's light/heavy vehicle distribution.
Hourly, weekly, monthly and yearly traffic statistics.
Train counts, passage times and durations.
Heatmap for busiest hours and days.

blocks.title: Export Word report
items: Open Analytics from the top toolbar.
Select the needed crossing on the left.
Click Download report.
Choose Today, 7 days, 30 days, 1 year or custom dates.
Click Download (.docx) and choose where to save the file.

blocks.title: Recommendation for official work
blocks.text: At the end of each month, save a 30-day report and export crossing settings as JSON backup.

blocks.title: Details on hover
blocks.text: Hold the cursor over any chart or map — exact numbers for that day, hour or cell appear. No need to read tiny labels.

blocks.title: Road condition map
items: One map, three signals: vehicles passed (number), road condition (colour), congestion cause (white dot).
Full description in the 'Road condition' section.

troubleshooting.lead: Use these checklists to quickly separate the most common operator issues.

blocks.title: Camera is not visible
items: Check RTSP URL, login and password.
Check that PC and camera are on the same network.
Test RTSP URL in VLC.
Click Refresh or disable/enable the camera.

blocks.title: Vehicles are not counted
items: Check that detection is enabled.
Wait until AI model is loaded.
Check that polygon is not too small or in the wrong place.
Check that camera image is not too dark, blurry or badly angled.

blocks.title: PLC does not connect
items: Check PLC IP and port.
Check network cable and switch.
Make sure PLC is not locked by another program.
If no connection continues, call IT or automation specialist.

blocks.title: Report is not exported
items: Check that selected date range has data.
Check write permission for the target folder.
Close the Word file if it is already open, then export again.

blocks.title: New questions
items: Box lags behind the vehicle — restart the program (an old version may be running).
Congestion map missing — dwell time is not collected yet; check the 'System status' section.
'Building engine' message on startup — a one-time step (2-5 minutes) that may repeat when the camera count changes.
If speed dropped after adding a camera — check that the engine is 'dynamic' in 'System status'.

integration.lead: RailSafe AI shares statistics with external systems in two ways: an external system reads FROM US (API server), or the app itself PUSHES data to a site. Both are managed from Settings → Integration — the section is password-protected, and no reinstall or rebuild is needed.

blocks.title: Enabling the API server (external system reads from us)
items: Open Settings → Integration tab. On first use you set a section password — only the responsible staff member should know it.
Turn on "API server". Optionally set the port (default 8750) and an API key, then press Save.
Verify: open http://localhost:8750/api/v1/health in a browser. No app restart is needed — the service reloads on save.

blocks.title: Available endpoints (GET, JSON)
items: /api/v1/health - server status and time.
/api/v1/crossings - list of crossings and cameras.
/api/v1/stats/today - today's totals for all crossings (light/heavy/trains).
/api/v1/stats/hourly?crossing_id=1 - 24-hour distribution (any day via date=).
/api/v1/stats/daily?crossing_id=1&from=2026-07-01&to=2026-07-20 - daily values for a period.
/api/v1/stats/weekly?crossing_id=1 and /api/v1/stats/monthly?crossing_id=1 - 7 days / 30 days.
/api/v1/trains/today?crossing_id=1 - today's train passes (count, duration).
/api/v1/trains/range?crossing_id=1&from=...&to=... - train passes for a period.

blocks.title: Automatic push to a site
items: Turn on Settings → Integration → "Automatic push to site".
Enter the site URL, login and password — the app obtains a token automatically and sends data at the chosen interval (default 5 minutes). It re-logins by itself when the token expires.
Use the "Test connection" button to try it immediately — the result is shown right there.
For the site developers: the "Save API sample" button exports the specification and a working sample server — they only need to build 2 endpoints.

blocks.title: Protection (API key)
items: If api_key is set, every request must include the X-API-Key header (or ?api_key= parameter) with that value.
If api_key is empty, the API is open - leave it that way only on a trusted local network.

blocks.title: Security note
items: The API returns statistics only - camera RTSP addresses and passwords are never exposed.
To connect from another computer, allow the chosen port (8750) in Windows Firewall.
Do not expose the API directly to the internet - use it on a local/corporate network or via VPN only.

version.lead: RailSafe AI is a local desktop product for railway crossing monitoring.

blocks.title: What's new (1.1.0)
items: INTEGRATION — API server for external systems (pull) and automatic push to a site; password-protected settings section, ready-made sample for developers
ANPR — license plate recognition during train passage (separate thread, no real-time impact)
DRAW the polygon (zone) directly on the camera frame — no file upload needed
Offline installer (setup.exe) — no Python/internet required; runs on CPU if no GPU
Word/PDF reports in three languages (uz/ru/en) + crossing CATEGORY (I-IV)
Improved window controls (minimize/maximize/resize) and stability

blocks.title: Product information
items: Product: RailSafe AI
Version: 1.1.0
Year: 2026
Organization: DAS-UTY LLC
Author: Muhammadiyev Bahrombek

blocks.title: Minimum requirements
items: Windows 10 or Windows 11, 64-bit.
Intel Core i5 8th gen or AMD Ryzen 5 and newer.
At least 8 GB RAM, 16 GB recommended.
NVIDIA GPU makes AI faster; CPU mode may work without GPU.
Cameras must be available by RTSP.
PLC and cameras must be on the same local network as the computer.

blocks.title: Recent improvements
items: Congestion grading now uses each vehicle's dwell time in the zone (vehicle count alone cannot detect a jam).
Load, congestion and zone utilization merged into ONE map; details appear on hover.
Detection box sits exactly on the vehicle — pipeline latency is compensated (important for ANPR accuracy).
The AI model adapts to the camera count by itself (dynamic engine) — no reconfiguration when a camera is added.
Hover tooltips on every chart; numbers are never clipped; colours follow the theme (light/dark/military).

road.lead: The road condition map shows 7 days x 24 hours in one table: the number in a cell is vehicles that passed, the colour is the road condition.

blocks.title: What the colours mean
items: Free (A) — road is clear, few vehicles.
Normal (B) — ordinary traffic.
Busy (C) — many vehicles but traffic flows.
Very busy (D) — close to capacity.
At capacity, stops (E) — a queue appears.
JAM — gridlock (F) — vehicles stand for a long time.

blocks.title: A small number with a red colour is not a bug
items: In a jam FEWER vehicles pass: flow drops while the road stays occupied.
So counting vehicles alone cannot detect a jam — in a full standstill the count falls to 0.
The system also uses a second measure: how long each vehicle STANDS in the zone. In a jam it grows several times over.
A white dot in the cell means the grade came from dwell time (few vehicles passed because they stood for a long time).

blocks.title: More detail
blocks.text: Hover a cell to see vehicles passed, dwell time per vehicle, how many minutes the zone was busy, and the condition name. Every chart works the same way — hover a bar or a point.

blocks.title: How thresholds are set
items: The scale is tied to the warning threshold in settings.
With a 30-second threshold: free up to 12s, busy up to 30s, very busy up to 45s, over 90s is a JAM.
Change the threshold in Settings > General.

blocks.title: Data has to accumulate
blocks.text: Dwell time is collected from the moment the program starts — it cannot be recomputed for past days. Until data exists, colour comes from vehicle count only and no white dots appear.

metrics.lead: The exact meaning of every number on the screen.

blocks.title: Vehicle counting
items: Light vehicles — cars and motorcycles.
Heavy vehicles — buses and trucks.
Total — light + heavy.
A vehicle is counted once when it ENTERS the zone; how long it stays does not affect the count.
The count resets to zero every midnight.

blocks.title: Zone metrics
items: Occupancy — how many vehicles are in the zone right now.
Zone time — time of the longest-standing vehicle; above the warning threshold it turns yellow, above the violation threshold red.
Dwell time (average) — how long a single vehicle stands in the zone; used for congestion grading.
Zone utilization — time when at least one vehicle was in the zone (min/hour). This is NOT a congestion measure: it is also high during busy but free-flowing hours.

blocks.title: Trains and PLC
items: Train count — from the PLC signal (barrier closing).
Duration — from signal on to signal off.
If the PLC is disabled, trains are not counted.

blocks.title: Technical metrics
items: FPS — frames processed per second.
Practical capacity (P) — 95th percentile of hourly flows over 30 days; load is measured against it.
Category (I-IV) — crossing category from the standard table, based on daily traffic and train count.

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.text: Hover any metric and a short version of this explanation appears right away.

system.lead: This section shows the CURRENT state of the program — send this information when you contact support.

blocks.title: Why it matters
items: If no GPU is found, AI runs slowly — you can see it here.
A 'fixed' engine loses speed when the camera count changes; a 'dynamic' one adapts by itself.
If dwell-time records are 'still collecting', the congestion map needs a day or two.
The log file (railsafe.log) helps find the cause of errors.
